items.title: Spain ends national emergency for wildfires near Madrid
items.summary: MADRID: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Thursday lifted the state of emergency over wildfires west of Madrid that forced the evacuations of tens of thousands of people. Authorities said the fires in the Madrid and Avila areas had stopped spreading and there are "almost no flames", a week after the emergency was declared, mobilising a national firefighting effort. But authorities warned that the ongoing heatwave threatened a resurgence of fire in the Madrid region.

items.title: Penang JPJ issues 1,328 summonses to foreign drivers under Ops PeWA since Jan 1
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, July 30 — The Penang Road Transport Department (JPJ) has issued 1,328 summonses to foreign drivers for various offences and impounded 178 vehicles under Op Khas Pemandu Warga Asing (PeWA) conducted since January 1. State JPJ director Zulkifly Ismail said that as of today, a total of 19,239 vehicles driven by foreigners were inspected, with enforcement action taken against 638 vehicles. “The operation is aimed at curbing offences involving foreign drivers who drive or operate motor vehicles without the required qualification, namely a valid driving licence.

items.title: Dewan Negara passes Social Work Profession Bill, establishes cross-sector council
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Dewan Negara today passed the Social Work Profession Bill 2026, which, among others, provides for the establishment of an inclusive Malaysian Social Work Profession Council comprising representatives from the government, private sector, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and academia. This means social work practitioners are assured of representation under the Act. She said the legislation is important to enhance the professionalism of the social work field, which is now facing increasingly complex social issues.

items.title: Philippines' Marcos approves release of VP Duterte's tax records to impeachment trial
items.summary: MANILA: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has approved the release of Vice President Sara Duterte's tax records to the Senate in her impeachment trial, where one of the charges she is facing is that she has amassed unexplained wealth while in office. Duterte has previously denied wrongdoing and called the impeachment proceedings politically motivated. The Senate, which is sitting as the impeachment court, will resume Duterte's trial on Aug 3.

items.title: Malaysia highways to get 77 new telecommunications towers to improve coverage, says works minister
items.summary: He said the target was among the outcomes of the memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed today between the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) to strengthen communications infrastructure along the country’s highway network. “In this context, cooperation between LLM and MCMC is crucial because the development of smart highways requires strong coordination between road infrastructure and communications infrastructure. Earlier, MCMC and LLM signed the MoU to strengthen strategic cooperation in developing communications infrastructure along the national highway network.

items.title: Penang’s Jalan Magazine to close for three days from Aug 7 for LRT works
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 30 — A section of Jalan Magazine towards Lebuh Carnarvon near Komtar here will be closed in stages for three days from August 7 to facilitate utility relocation works for the Light Rail Transit (LRT) Mutiara Line Project. According to a Penang Mutiara Line (PML) project statement today, the closure will take place from 10pm on Friday (August 7) until 5am on Monday (August 10), involving three lanes between the Capri Hotel and The Magazine Hotel construction areas. The closure is required for preliminary works under the LRT Mutiara Line Project Package CMC1, involving utility relocation by the Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP).

items.title: Starlink to trial satellite-to-phone internet service in Malaysia, says Fahmi
items.summary: CYBERJAYA, July 30 — Satellite internet provider Starlink plans to conduct a trial of its direct-to-device (D2D), or direct-to-cell, technology in Malaysia, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said the technology has the potential to deliver internet connectivity directly to mobile phones via satellite in selected areas without relying on telecommunications towers. Also present were Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi, Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching, Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and Works Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Azman Ibrahim.

items.title: KTMB records strong growth in first half of 2026, revenue increases to RM296mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) recorded 13.2 million passengers in the first half of 2026, an increase of eight per cent compared to the same period last year. Its group chief executive officer, Datuk Azlan Shah Al Bakri said the increase also contributed to the company's total revenue from RM206 million to RM296 million. He said the growth was driven primarily by the excellent performance of the Electric Train Service (ETS), which recorded a 55 per cent increase in the number of passengers, from two million to 3.1 million, in addition to the Intercity service with 2.1 million passengers.

items.title: Zayn Rayyan case: High Court to hear mother Ismanira’s appeal against five-year jail term on Aug 19
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 30 — The High Court today set August 19 to hear Ismanira Abdul Manaf’s appeal against her conviction and five-year prison sentence for neglecting her six-year-old son, Zayn Rayyan Abdul Matin, resulting in physical injury three years ago. Judge Noor Hisham Ismail set the date after deputy public prosecutor Raja Zaizul Faridah Raja Zaharudin informed the court that the prosecution required time to file further submissions in response to the defence’s additional arguments. Counsel Haresh Mahadevan, representing Ismanira, raised no objection.

items.title: UPSI student clinches bronze at Adobe World Championship
items.summary: TANJUNG MALIM: A Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris (UPSI) student brought pride to Malaysia when he finished third at the prestigious Adobe Certified Professional (ACP) World Championship in Anaheim, California. Muhammad Fawwaz Haiqal Mohd Fuaad, a student at UPSI's Faculty of Computing and Meta Technology (Meta), beat 200 other participants from 45 countries in the international competition held yesterday. "His success places UPSI and Malaysia on the world map as a producer of high-calibre digital talent.

items.title: Police cripple illegal Bitcoin mining operation in Batu Gajah
items.summary: BATU GAJAH: Police have crippled an illegal Bitcoin mining operation in Tronoh, with the arrest of two men and the seizure of 73 cryptocurrency mining machines believed to have been powered by stolen electricity. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Md Noor Aehawan Mohammad said the raids were carried out at three premises at 9.02pm on Tuesday under Op Elektrik, following intelligence gathering and surveillance. "Investigations found that all three premises were carrying out Bitcoin mining activities using illegal electricity connections.

items.title: Anwar congratulates Aliff Rakib on ONE Muay Thai world title win
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Muay Thai fighter Aliff Rakib on his historic achievement of becoming the first Malaysian to win the ONE Interim Muay Thai Strawweight World Championship. Anwar said he received Aliff at his office and congratulated him on the milestone. "Congratulations Aliff, Malaysia is proud of this achievement," he said in a Facebook post today.

items.title: MACC forms task force to review Tabung Haji RCI report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has formed a special task force to review the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH) following its public release. MACC said its Investigation Division senior director Datuk Mohd Hafaz Nazar had been appointed to lead the special task force. "The team will scrutinise the report for any offences under the MACC Act, the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act, or any other relevant laws," MACC said in a statement.

items.title: Trust: New currency of the AI era
items.summary: UNLIKE previous technological revolutions, artificial intelligence (AI) is not simply changing how we work. Yet institutions alone do not build AI nations. Trust does.

items.title: Negri polls: Vote-buying allegations unfair, says Aminuddin
items.summary: PORT DICKSON: Negri Sembilan Pakatan Harapan chairman Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has described allegations linking the coalition to vote-buying as unfair. He said such accusations should not be directed at any single political party, as no one knows who was behind the alleged vote-buying. I think Datuk Jalal's (Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias ) accusation yesterday should not be directed at a single political party.

items.title: Anwar lauds Maybank's transformation into regional banking leader
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has praised Maybank's transformation into one of Asia's leading financial institutions. He said the bank's success is underpinned not only by strong financial performance but also by sound governance and integrity. Speaking at the opening of Maybank's new headquarters, Menara Merdeka Maybank, today, Anwar described the banking group as a national landmark and a symbol of Malaysia's economic progress.

items.title: Jamil Khir says TH decisions were based on board recommendations
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Former Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom said he never acted beyond the investment recommendations submitted by the Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) Board during his tenure overseeing the institution from 2009 to 2018. Jamil Khir said TH operates under the government's governance framework and that the minister cannot approve any application, request, sale or purchase of assets, or leasing matters unless they are first recommended by TH. "The minister's authority is based on the board's recommendations," he said.

items.title: Rais Yatim accepts withdrawal of Negri honours with 'open heart'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Negri Sembilan menteri besar Tan Sri Rais Yatim has accepted the withdrawal of two Negri Sembilan honours "with an open heart". In a video posted on TikTok by @minaq_jinggo, Rais said he had received notification that the Negri Sembilan palace had withdrawn the Datuk Seri Utama and Datuk honours today. "Seasons change and honours are conferred.

items.title: Man pleads not guilty over foster mother's RM182,223 account misuse
items.summary: ROMPIN: A food stall helper pleaded not guilty at the Magistrate's Court here today to charges of dishonestly using RM182,223 from his foster mother's account, as well as unlawfully possessing her debit card. Mohamad Nor Farazul Mohamed, 37, who faces four charges, including two related to drug offences, entered his plea before magistrate Melody Woon Sze Mun. Nor Farazul was accused of possessing a bank debit card belonging to a 69-year-old woman without lawful authority on July 28 at a stall in Taman Seri Maulana, Pekan.

items.title: Driver charged with murder over Teluk Intan crash killing two teenage schoolgirls
items.summary: TELUK INTAN, July 30 — The car driver involved in a road crash that claimed the lives of two teenage girls on Jalan Padang Tembak here last Sunday was charged in the Magistrates’ Court today with four offences, including two counts of murder. Under the first charge, Alex is accused of murdering 17-year-old Nur Dania Arissa Salim near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Seri Setia on Jalan Padang Tembak at 6.35pm on July 26. The second charge alleges that he murdered 16-year-old Nur Atikah Abdullah at the same location, date and time.

items.title: Bursa backs expanding FBM KLCI to 50 constituents
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia Bhd has backed a proposal to expand the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) from 30 to 50 constituents in a move to better reflect the breadth of the domestic equity market. The proposal, issued jointly by Bursa Malaysia and global index provider FTSE Russell for market consultation, forms part of a broader review of the methodology for the FBM KLCI and the FTSE Bursa Malaysia Mid 70 Index (FBM70). Chief executive officer Datuk Fad'l Mohamed said the expansion would broaden market coverage, strengthen sector representation and reduce concentration risks, particularly in the financial services sector.

items.title: Ayob Khan on the Nicky Liow investigation: "It was one of Bukit Aman's biggest cases"
items.summary: The recently retired police was the leader of an investigation involving Nicky Liow when he was the Johor police chief. Liow was later charged but eventually acquitted of 26 money laundering charges involving more than RM36 million after the prosecution withdrew the case four years ago. [[nid:1500575]] The case involving Liow became a defining moment in Ayob's fight against organised crime as it was not merely a police operation, but a test of leadership, courage and institutional integrity.

items.title: Special Parliament sitting on Tabung Haji RCI report set for Aug 11, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim revealed that the special parliamentary sitting on Tabung Haji’s Royal Commision of Inquiry (RCI) report will be held on August 11. “A special parliamentary session will be held this August 11. “The session will begin from 10am until the evening,” Anwar said.

items.title: MSMEs GDP grows 5.7pct in 2025, outpaces overall economy
items.summary: The services and manufacturing sectors remained the largest contributors to MSMEs' GDP, accounting for a combined 84.5 per cent, followed by agriculture (8.4 per cent), construction (5.3 per cent) and mining and quarrying (0.5 per cent). The construction sector grew 12.0 per cent in 2025, compared with 17.5 per cent a year earlier, while mining and quarrying expanded 4.4 per cent, against 4.8 per cent in 2024. The increase was driven by manufacturing and services exports, which grew 8.8 per cent (2024: 7.9 per cent) and 14.0 per cent (2024: 106.6 per cent), respectively.

items.title: Anwar calls for banks to 'humanise' financial services
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on financial institutions to go beyond profitability by ensuring greater access to quality financial services for all Malaysians. Anwar said financial institutions must embrace the concept of "humanising financial services" by balancing commercial success with social responsibility. "Democracy means democratisation of access; access to quality services, financial services and education," he said at the opening of Maybank's new headquarters at Menara Merdeka Maybank today.

items.title: Starlink eyes Malaysia for direct-to-cell internet trial
items.summary: CYBERJAYA: Telecommunications giant Starlink is looking to conduct trials of its direct-to-device satellite internet technology in Malaysia. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said this could potentially expand internet access to areas without telecommunications towers, particularly sparsely populated locations. Last year, however, Fahmi had said Putrajaya was exploring alternative options to reduce its reliance on Starlink's low-earth orbit satellite internet service, operated by SpaceX, the company founded by billionaire Elon Musk.

items.title: 77 telco towers planned to boost highway coverage
items.summary: CYBERJAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will build 77 telecommunications towers along 50km of highway stretches nationwide identified as having poor mobile coverage. "MCMC is targeting the construction of 77 new telecommunications towers along 50km of highway stretches identified as having unsatisfactory coverage," he said at the memorandum of understanding (MoU) exchange ceremony between MCMC and the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA) today. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, who also attended the ceremony, said MCMC had issued a tender on May 15 to improve internet coverage through the construction of telecommunications towers along 10 MHA-managed highways with weak connectivity.

items.title: New UK PM urged to put food on a par with defence and energy
items.summary: LONDON: A fresh food shock in Britain is only a matter of time after years of disruptions that have driven up prices, more than 100 organisations said in a letter urging new Prime Minister Andy Burnham to make food a national priority alongside defence and energy. Signatories, including food retailers Tesco and Sainsbury's and dairy producer Danone, called on Burnham to urgently introduce a "Good Food Bill" to improve food security, resilience and public health. To meet it prepared, food has to stop being an afterthought for the Government," the letter, organised by charity the Food Foundation, said.

items.title: Estate planning key to protecting family wealth, say experts
items.summary: They said changing family structures, increasing cross-border investments, digital assets and a growing intergenerational wealth transfer make estate planning more important than ever. "Estate planning goes beyond drafting a will. It also includes trusts, hibah, powers of attorney and succession planning," she said.

items.title: Maybank launches Menara Merdeka headquarters [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's largest bank, Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), has officially launched its new headquarters at Menara Merdeka Maybank, officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Maybank said the new headquarters reflects its commitment to the future by bringing its corporate functions under one roof. "Maybank remains a strong financial institution, recognised across Asia, supported by the people of Malaysia, and has earned its place as one of the region's most respected financial institutions," he said in a speech.

items.title: Elon Musk's Starlink eyes direct-to-device satellite internet trials in Malaysia
items.summary: CYBERJAYA: Telecommunications giant Starlink is looking to conduct trials of its direct-to-device, or direct-to-cell, satellite internet technology in Malaysia. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said this could potentially expand internet access to areas without telecommunications towers, particularly in sparsely populated locations. "This is a significant technological advancement because it means we can provide internet connectivity via satellite to certain areas that do not have telecommunications towers, particularly locations with low population density," he said.

items.title: Ukraine targets Russia online retailer facilities
items.summary: MOSCOW: Two warehouses belonging to the Russian online retail giant Wildberries, were targeted overnight by new Ukrainian drone attacks, the company and local authorities said Thursday. Another Wildberries warehouse was hit by a Ukrainian drone in Sarapul, about 1,100 km (685 miles) east of Moscow, and a fire broke out, according to the company. Staff were evacuated and "according to preliminary information, no one was injured," Wildberries said Ukraine first targeted Wildberries warehouses on July 18-19 in the Tambov region about 480 km southeast of the Russian capital, as well as in the Moscow region, resulting in eight casualties and destroying facilities.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar confirms Aug 11 special Dewan Rakyat sitting to discuss TH RCI report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has confirmed that a special Dewan Rakyat sitting to discuss the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH) will be held on Aug 11. Anwar said he had discussed the matter with Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Dr Johari Abdul, who agreed to convene the special sitting. "Aug 11, special parliament sitting.

items.title: Committee overseeing haj operations needs statutory status, says Tabung Haji RCI
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has recommended that the Haj Affairs Committee be given statutory status under the Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535) and assigned specific responsibilities. According to the RCI report released yesterday, the committee was established to assess and decide on matters relating to haj operations after the Haj Advisory Council was dissolved in 2018 following the repeal of the Tabung Haji Board Act 1969 (Act 8). The RCI proposed that the Haj Affairs Committee advise the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) on policies and planning related to haj affairs, as well as deliberate on issues concerning the welfare of pilgrims and other matters referred to it in relation to haj operations.

items.title: Asyraf Wajdi: Tabung Haji RCI report debate will ensure accountability
items.summary: PORT DICKSON: The tabling of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH) in Parliament for debate will ensure that all parties involved are held accountable. Welcoming the release of the report, Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the party had, from the outset, called for the establishment of an RCI to investigate all allegations raised against Tabung Haji. Asyraf Wajdi said all findings disclosed in the report should be debated in Parliament.

items.title: PDC to develop Batu Kawan Industrial Park 2 after failed tender rounds
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Development Corporation (PDC) will develop the Batu Kawan Industrial Park 2 project itself after three requests for proposals and tender exercises failed. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the decision was made by the PDC board on July 20, allowing the agency to have full control over the development of the strategic industrial park. Chow said PDC had yet to focus on marketing the industrial park or securing investors as its immediate priority was to complete site preparation works.

items.title: Ex-Tabung Haji CEO questions silence after RCI report emerges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chief executive officer Datuk Nik Mohd Hasyudeen Yusoff has taken aim at critics following the declassification of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into the institution's management and operations. Hasyudeen said critics had been quick to react to unproven allegations but remained silent when facts emerged. The RCI report examined Hasyudeen's removal as TH chief executive officer on May 5, 2021, months before his extended contract was due to expire on Aug 31.

items.title: Home Ministry starts refugee checks as Malaysia prepares to send back 5,000 Myanmar nationals
items.summary: BUKIT KAYU HITAM, July 30 — The Home Ministry (KDN) has begun identifying, documenting and screening Rohingya refugees as part of preparations to repatriate 5,000 Myanmar nationals after the Myanmar government agreed to accept the return of its citizens currently in Malaysia. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the process was being carried out through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) in line with National Security Council (MKN) Directive No. He said the DPP process involved several stages, including tracing, identification, security screening and determining the status of each individual before confirmation documents were issued.

items.title: Israeli strikes kill three in Gaza, including two children, amid new ceasefire talks
items.summary: CAIRO: Israeli strikes killed at least three people, including two children, in the Gaza Strip on Thursday, health officials said, as mediators held new talks with Hamas leaders to work towards full implementation of a US-brokered Gaza peace plan. The Israeli military said both strikes targeted Hamas fighters. Hamas does not usually disclose its losses.

items.title: As polling day nears, what’s on Negeri Sembilan voters’ minds?
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 30 — Over the past decade, Aina Mohamed, 33, has watched Negeri Sembilan evolve, with new public facilities, businesses and housing developments changing parts of the state that once felt much quieter. The Negeri Sembilan native, who lives in Ampangan, said the changes were easy to spot, from the opening of the Urban Transformation Centre (UTC) and new commercial areas to the transformation of towns across the state. Alongside the state’s physical growth, she said she had also noticed changes in how communities interact.

items.title: Love scams and fake investments cost Terengganu RM21m in first half of 2026
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, July 30 — Terengganu continues to record an increase in commercial crime cases, with 1,009 cases recorded in the first six months of this year compared to 995 cases during the same period last year. Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said cybercrime accounted for the highest number of cases at 980; followed by counterfeit currency (13 cases); offences under the Moneylenders Act 1951 (Amendment 2011) (12 cases); criminal breach of trust (three cases); and other cases (one case). He said that commercial crime cases this year also recorded an increase in total losses, rising from RM20,198,493.73 between January and June last year to RM21,035,250.57 during the same period this year.

items.title: Heart op recovery keeps Najib from court in bid to revive suit against ex-AG Thomas, but majority grants delay — with a warning
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 30 — In a 2-1 majority decision, the Apex Court today granted Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak’s application to adjourn the hearing of his leave bid to revive his RM1.9 million civil suit against former Attorney-General (AG) Tan Sri Tommy Thomas after being told that the former prime minister was recovering from a heart procedure. A three-member panel comprising Federal Court judges Datuk Seri Abu Bakar Jais and Datuk Azmi Ariffin formed the majority, while Justice Datuk Azimah Omar dissented. “Najib is unwell and, under the circumstances, I am allowing this application,” he said.

items.title: Sabah sets aside RM100m for scholarships, targets future healthcare talent
items.summary: Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Haji Noor said the Sabah State Government Scholarship (BKNS) allocation will cover existing recipients as well as new sponsorships for 2026, involving 2,182 students, with emphasis on strategic fields including science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM). Hajiji, who is also chairman of the Yayasan Sabah board of trustees, said education remained a priority for the state government as the foundation for producing skilled and competitive human capital. He said the government had also expanded other education assistance programmes, including the Sabah State Government Excellent Scholarship, the B40 and Rural Programme Scholarship, as well as financial aid schemes aimed at easing the burden of higher education costs.

items.title: Pakatan demands accountability over Tabung Haji misconduct, calls to prosecute without compromise
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 30 — The government must act swiftly to restore public confidence in Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) and safeguard the rights of depositors following the release of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into the pilgrim fund, Pakatan Harapan (PH) said. “PH commends the government for releasing the Tabung Haji RCI report, which clearly demonstrates its continued commitment to good governance, accountability and transparency,” he said in a statement today. Saifuddin said the government under Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had successfully restored TH’s financial management, noting that 75 per cent of the RCI’s recommendations had already been implemented.

items.title: RCI pushes for new Haj Fund dept to safeguard Tabung Haji’s future as deposits approach RM100b
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has recommended the establishment of a dedicated department known as the Haj Fund under TH to manage depositors’ funds, with oversight by the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) to enhance investment management professionalism. The RCI said the move would allow TH to retain its investment management functions rather than be placed under a separate subsidiary. The TH Board would appoint senior officers, including the chief investment officer, who would be supervised by the SC.

items.title: Abdul Azeez says ready to face fresh probe over Tabung Haji RCI findings
items.summary: JELEBU, July 30 — Former Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim said he is prepared to be investigated again if necessary following allegations of misconduct raised in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report, according to Sinar Harian. Abdul Azeez said the 204-page RCI report had been completed at the end of 2022 and tabled at several Cabinet meetings. Abdul Azeez said he had previously appealed to then prime minister Dr Mahathir, then deputy prime minister Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail and former minister in the Prime Minister’s Department Datuk Seri Mujahid Yusof Rawa to establish an RCI into the matter.

items.title: Are Malaysia’s small traders ready for Asean’s digital economy? Yes, even fried banana sellers use QR codes, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — Malaysia's micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) are well positioned to tap Asean's 680-million-consumer market under the proposed Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA), supported by their high level of digital adoption, Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said. He said harmonising digital regulatory frameworks would reduce market fragmentation, creating a more efficient, cost-effective and globally competitive Asean digital economic bloc. Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin is confident that Malaysia’s micro, small and medium enterprises are ready for Asean’s cross-border digital trade.

items.title: RM1,000 subsidy and a new centre: How Malaysia is stepping up support for kids with autism as registrations rise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — About 93,000 of the 850,000 persons with disabilities (PwDs) registered with the Department of Social Welfare (JKM) as of June this year are those with autism, the Dewan Negara was told today. Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying said the increase in registrations had prompted the government to enhance various initiatives on early intervention, education and skills training for the group. “Recently, the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) established an Autism Service Centre in Bangi with the primary objective of providing a one-stop centre offering quality, affordable and easily accessible services,” she said when replying to a question from Senator Dr A. Lingeshwaran.

items.title: Agriculture Ministry says Malaysia imports too much ginger, mangoes, rice and fresh milk — here’s what’s changing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — The Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM) is focusing on increasing the production of agri-food commodities with low Self-Sufficiency Ratio (SSR) levels to reduce the country’s dependence on food imports. Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin said commodities that still require attention include ginger, with an SSR of 15.5 per cent, mangoes (20 per cent), rice (about 52 per cent) and fresh milk (66.7 per cent). Meanwhile, in response to concerns over food supply to rural areas in Sabah and Sarawak, Chan said KPKM is working with PLANMalaysia to develop the National Food Source Area Land Use Planning Master Plan to safeguard food production areas.

items.title: Money laundering charges: Former GISB chief, three ex-accountants to learn fate of representations on Oct 3
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 30 — The Sessions Court today fixed Oct 3 to decide on representations submitted by former GISB Holdings Sdn Bhd (GISBH) chief executive officer Nasiruddin Mohd Ali and three former company accountants in relation to 331 money laundering charges involving more than RM38.1 million. The four accused are Nasiruddin, 67, who faces 77 charges involving more than RM10 million; Hamimah Yakub, 74, who faces 95 charges involving RM11.4 million; Asmat @ Asmanira Muhammad Ramly, 46, who faces 68 charges involving RM4.7 million; and Mohd Khushairi Osman, 55, who faces 91 charges involving nearly RM12 million. Counsel Muhammad Zaim Rosli appeared for Nasiruddin, Asmat @ Asmanira and Mohd Khushairi.

items.title: Govt to speed up remaining Tabung Haji reform recommendations, says Islamic Affairs minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — The government will expedite the implementation of the remaining 25 per cent of recommendations by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), taking into account current realities and other relevant considerations, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan. On the recommendation to restructure TH’s governance, he said he was open to considering the proposal, including separating responsibilities for financial, fund and investment management under the Finance Minister. Zulkifli said the recommendation to limit the scope of the Religious Affairs Minister’s authority to haj management was among the suggestions contained in the RCI report published yesterday.

items.title: UMS, industry partner to develop sustainable battery-free lighting system in Sabah
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, July 30 — A RM76,000 research project to develop a battery-free lighting system powered by thermal energy will be carried out in Sabah under the Industrial Collaboration Programme (ICP). The project, involving Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) and Seni Gemilang Sdn Bhd, aims to advance sustainable energy research while developing a Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) learning module for schools in Sabah. The ICP is a government initiative led by the Ministry of Finance that uses selected government procurement projects to encourage technology adoption, research partnerships, innovation and talent development.

items.title: Putrajaya plans two new infertility clinics nationwide yearly to help low-income couples
items.summary: Deputy Minister Lim Hui Ying said the move aims to expand access to quality and affordable subfertility services, particularly to assist married couples from lower-income groups. She said fertility treatment services under the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN) are currently provided through four main zonal clinics, namely in Penang (Northern Zone), Kuala Lumpur (Central Zone), Johor Bahru (Southern Zone) and Kuching (East Malaysia Zone). Lim said the Buai Programme comprises two initiatives, namely subsidies for treatment fees, including medication and procedures, as well as advocacy programmes to increase participants’ understanding and knowledge.

items.title: One twin dead, one survives: Johor cops arrest college student and boyfriend over newborn's murder in Kluang toilet
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, July 30 — Police have arrested a 19-year-old college student and her boyfriend of the same age to assist in the investigation into the murder of a newborn baby girl found with multiple stab wounds at a rented house in Taman Setia Mutiara, Kluang, yesterday. Johor Police Chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said police received a report at 1 pm after the woman was admitted to Enche Besar Hajjah Khalsom Hospital following childbirth. The baby was subsequently delivered safely,” he told a press conference at the Johor Police Headquarters today.

items.title: Penang CM: Sungai Nibong TOD master plan expected to be finalised in October
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 30 — The draft Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Master Plan for Sungai Nibong is expected to be finalised in October, said Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. He said the state government is currently conducting engagement sessions with various stakeholders to gather feedback before finalising the master plan. Chow said the implementation phase would be the challenging part and was projected to take between 10 and 15 years.

items.title: Verify all state-owned land deals first, Pahang tells public after fraud case in Bentong
items.summary: KUANTAN, July 30 — The Pahang government has uncovered a land application fraud syndicate in the Bentong district involving state-owned land. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the syndicate offered land alienation services by asking members of the public to make payments and sign documents before the process was carried out. “I would like to emphasise that the Pahang government has not appointed any individual, agent or company to handle the alienation of state government land outside the procedures stipulated by law.

items.title: Penang mulls holding Pesta Pulau Pinang in Seberang Perai this year
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 30 — The Penang state government is considering organising the annual Pesta Pulau Pinang at Seberang Perai towards the end of this year. Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the cultural festival could be held on a smaller scale in North Seberang Perai. On the original Pesta site in Sungai Nibong, Chow said the draft Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Master Plan covers about 23.47 hectares (58 acres).

items.title: Adibah Amin’s writings should be taught in schools to promote unity, says UM pro-chancellor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — The works of acclaimed Malaysian journalist, writer and educator Adibah Amin should be incorporated into the school curriculum to instil the values of unity, tolerance and nationhood among younger generations, former Federal Court Judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali said. The Universiti Malaya Pro-Chancellor said Adibah’s writings remained highly relevant as Malaysia continued to navigate issues of race, religion and social cohesion. Adibah Amin’s As I Was Passing belongs squarely to the latter,” she said.

items.title: Penang says DOSM tourism survey does not reflect full visitor numbers
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 30 — Penang’s tourism and creative economy committee chairman Wong Hon Wai today said the Department of Statistics Malaysia’s (DOSM) Domestic Tourism Survey 2025 should not be treated as a definitive measure of the state’s tourism performance as it was based on a sample survey. He said the survey also included day trippers and those travelling interstate to visit family members. Wong said actual hotel accommodation data provided a more reliable indicator of tourism performance.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan palace revokes two titles awarded to Rais Yatim
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 30 — The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has ordered the immediate revocation of the Darjah Seri Utama Negeri Sembilan (SPNS) and Darjah Dato’ Setia Negeri Sembilan (DSNS) awards conferred on Tan Sri Dr Mohd Rais Yatim. Negeri Sembilan Awards Registrar Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim said in a statement issued today that the decision was made to preserve the dignity, honour and prestige of the Negri Sembilan Royal Institution. “The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan has ordered the revocation of the Darjah Seri Utama Negeri Sembilan (SPNS) (2001) and Darjah Dato’ Setia Negeri Sembilan (DSNS) (1979) awards conferred on Tan Sri Dr Mohd Rais Yatim, effective immediately,” he said.
